_comment: My league. Update my_score/opponent_scores from the site standings each week.
opponent_scores may be left empty; then num_opponents players are assumed tied with me.
field_sharpness controls how herd-like the other players are:
1.0 = they hold my exact read, 2.5 = typical (they pile onto the obvious boot),
5.0 = near-unanimous consensus. Raise it once you can see their picks.
Confirmed from data/site/standings.txt, read from a real signed-in session on 2026-09-17.
3 opponents, all tied at 0 before episode 1: Claude's Fleshbag (tribe name)
/ JCPenny (username), Claude Spoiler Bot 2000 / Claude-Bot, Touch Copper /
aaaaaaaaaaaa. field_sharpness/field_all_in_fraction/field_noise are still
the pre-season defaults - none of these three have voted yet, so there is
nothing real to raise or lower them from.
Their Sole Survivor picks are already public (data/site/standings.txt,
'league activity'): Claude's Fleshbag -> Carter, Claude Spoiler Bot 2000 ->
Thien An, Touch Copper -> Jenna. The engine does not use this - the vote
simulation only models weekly vote points, not the Sole Survivor pick -
but it means none of them currently hold Eric, our pick.
num_opponents/opponent_scores/opponent_names ARE the current live count.
'python3 tools/submit.py standings' rebuilds these three fields from
however many rows actually exist on the site each time it runs - it is
always honest about who has actually joined right now, nothing more.
expected_min_opponents is a SEPARATE field, untouched by that sync. The
user confirmed on 2026-09-18 that not everyone who will join this league
has signed up yet (the site exposes no 'pending invites' count to check
this independently), then told us directly the expected final roster:
5-6 real people, one other bot, and this account - i.e. 6-7 opponents
total. Set to 6, the low end of that range. fsb/allocate.py's
effective_opponent_scores() pads opponent_scores up to this minimum
(with phantom opponents tied at my_score, the same assumption already
used when opponent_scores is empty) so the win-probability simulation
does not under-count the field just because real signups are still
trickling in. Once the live sync's real count reaches or passes 6, this
field stops doing anything - raise it only if the user reports a new
expected total.
_field_evidence: Vote points scored by the 8 players: 6, 5, and zero for the other six (me included).
Two readings follow. The field is NOT herd-like: nobody piled onto one obvious
name hard enough to take the full 10, and the castaway who actually went was not
the consensus pre-season pick. And the field is NOT accurate: three quarters of
it scored nothing. So sharpness drops 2.5 -> 1.8, all-in 0.7 -> 0.5 (both of the
players who scored spread their points rather than going all in), and noise rises
0.6 -> 0.8. Net effect: against a field this noisy, being right is worth more than
being different, so the optimiser should sit closer to the true favourite.
One episode is thin evidence - revisit these after episode 2 and 3.
